run.executedVia: Playwright (automated), driving the /shiftpay Service Portal; every screen assertion cross-checked against the ServiceNow Table API.

case.title: Logging a day writes one row and re-aggregates with a rate snapshot

steps.text: Log UK on 2026-10-01 with a comment, and confirm the chip renders.
screenshots: C:\Users\patel\Documents\ServiceNow Work Project Docs\Personal AI Assisted\ShiftPay Clean Vibe coding\testing\automation\evidence\TC-SP-002\01-day-logged.png

steps.text: Read the submission row the save produced.
Read the recomputed week summary and check the arithmetic.
Clear 2026-10-01 and confirm both the row and the aggregate revert.

observations: The rate is asserted as u_rate_snapshot on the summary row, not as the live catalogue rate. The snapshot is what payroll pays and what a manager approves, so a catalogue change after aggregation must not move it — reading the live rate would hide it if that ever broke.

Aggregates are recomputed rather than incremented: ShiftPayAggregator deletes and rewrites the affected week and month rows per shift type, which is why clearing the day removes the row outright instead of leaving a zero-count orphan.
expected: Saving produces exactly one u_shift_submission row for that user and date, with the chosen shift type and the typed comment.
A week summary row exists for the Monday of that week with u_rate_snapshot equal to the catalogue rate and u_amount = u_count x u_rate_snapshot.
Clearing the day removes the submission row and reverts the summary.
actual: 1 submission row(s) for 2026-10-01; week of 2026-09-28 now counts 1 UK shift(s) at a snapshot of 350.
After clearing: 0 submission row(s), week count back to 0 (was 0 before the run).
case.verdictReason: One row written and removed cleanly; the week aggregate moved to 1 at a snapshot of 350 and back to 0.
